title: Randomized Kriging Believer For Parallel Bayesian Optimization With Regret Bounds
claim: Conditioning on fantasized outcomes at pending evaluations steers each new selection away from redundant points, keeping parallel choices diverse.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right by iteration, shared legend on top, acquisition curve beneath
description: A shared legend runs across the top. It covers black observed data, cyan fantasized data, dashed black lines for inputs being evaluated, a red line for the next evaluation, and blue and orange curves with shaded bands for the predictive and fantasized predictive mean and uncertainty. Below it are three side-by-side panels titled Iteration 1, 2 and 3. Each panel is a 1-D Gaussian-process sketch: objective versus input, with an acquisition-function (AF) curve in a short strip underneath. Iteration 1 shows only the blue posterior and a red line at the AF maximum. In iterations 2 and 3, dashed lines mark pending inputs with cyan fantasized points on them. An orange posterior and band appear around those points, and the red line shifts to a different region. The eye goes first to the red and dashed vertical lines and the colored bands.
caption: Schematic illustration of the proposed method for three consecutive iterations. For efficient parallel optimization, it is necessary to evaluate diverse input points while avoiding redundant evaluation. The left figure shows iteration 1, where no inputs are under evaluation, and thus, the next input is chosen as in standard BO. The middle and right figures show iterations 2 and 3, respectively. There are inputs currently being evaluated, indicated by dashed lines. In these cases, RKB generates fantasized data from the predictive distribution at the inputs under evaluation. Then, the next input is selected by maximizing an AF based on a model trained on both observed (real) and fantasized data. As a result, BO avoids redundant evaluation and ensures diversity among the evaluated inputs.
abstract: We consider the optimization problem of an expensive-to-evaluate black-box function, in which we can obtain noisy function values in parallel. For this problem, parallel Bayesian optimization (PBO) is a promising approach, which aims to optimize with fewer function evaluations by selecting a diverse input set for parallel evaluation. However, existing PBO methods suffer from poor practical performance or lack theoretical guarantees. In this study, we propose a PBO method, called randomized kriging believer (KB), based on a well-known KB heuristic and inheriting the advantages of the original KB: low computational complexity, a simple implementation, versatility across various BO methods, and applicability to asynchronous parallelization. Furthermore, we show that our randomized KB achieves Bayesian expected regret guarantees. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method through experiments, including those on real-data emulators.
